subject: choiceNames and choiceValues in mirtCAT shinyGUI object do not appear to work

messages.author: 51b9e9969e604449
messages.subject: choiceNames and choiceValues in mirtCAT shinyGUI object do not appear to work
parts:
Hi Phil,

I hope you're doing well. 

I'm currently developing a CAT version of an existing personality measure where respondents are presented with two traits, and are asked to rate themselves on a spectrum between the two. For example, an item might present Lively on the left and Shy on the right, and response options will be something like "Certainly describes me", "Somewhat describes me"," Both describe me equally well", "Somewhat describes me", and "Certainly describes me". 

I was hoping to set up the CAT GUI to parse the above response options as 1,2,3,4, & 5 respectively. However, when I supply lists to the choiceNames and choiceValues parameters in the shinyGUI object, the CAT does not seem to behave any differently and still presents the options included in the main df object.

Here is a small reproducible example using the short 3-item non-adaptive test that you include in some of your tutorials:

options <- matrix(c(1,2,3,4,5),
                  nrow = 3, ncol = 5, byrow = TRUE)
questions <- c("Building CATs with mirtCAT is difficult.",
               "mirtCAT requires a substantial amount of coding.",
               "I would use mirtCAT in my research.")

df<-data.frame(Question=questions,Option=options,Type="radio")

list.values<-vector(mode="list",length=3)
for(i in 1:3){
  list.values[[i]]<-c(1,2,3,4,5)
}

list.names<-vector(mode="list",length=3)
for(i in 1:3){
  list.names[[i]]<-c("Strongly Disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly Agree")
}

results<-mirtCAT(df=df, shinyGUI=list(choiceNames=list.names, choiceValues=list.values))


When I run the mirtCAT() line, I expected the response options to be presented as c("Strongly Disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly Agree"), raw responses to come from c("Strongly Disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly Agree"), and scored responses to be integers. Instead, 1,2,3,4,5 are presented as the response options, and recorded as raw responses, with the scored responses recorded as NAs like below.

str(results)
List of 13
 $ login_name            : chr(0) 
 $ raw_responses         : chr [1:3] "1" "3" "5"
 $ scored_responses      : logi [1:3] NA NA NA
 $ items_answered        : int [1:3] 1 2 3
 $ thetas                : logi NA
 $ SE_thetas             : logi NA
 $ thetas_history        : logi NA
 $ thetas_SE_history     : logi NA
 $ item_time             : num [1:3] 0 0 0
 $ demographics          :'data.frame': 0 obs. of  0 variables
 $ terminated_sucessfully: logi TRUE
 $ GUI                   : logi TRUE
 $ clientData            :List of 6

I'm hoping this example generalizes to an adaptive test for your purposes. On my end the same issue is present for adaptive and non-adaptive tests, with the exception that scored responses are the same as the raw responses, rather than NAs.

Any idea how to fix this? Perhaps there are columns I could manually add to the df object that indicate that the recorded value and presented label are different? Or maybe there's a column I can add that tells mirtCAT to look at the choiceNames and choiceValues rather than at df$Option.1 through df$Option.5? 

Best,

Jordan

messages.subject: Re: choiceNames and choiceValues in mirtCAT shinyGUI object do not appear to work
parts:
Hi Jordan,

Apologies for the long overdue response. 

I don't quite see the need for the choiceName and choiceValue inputs in this example as this information should be defined in the more canonical df object, but the fix in this case is largely due to poor documentation. The choiceName/choiceValue inputs must be a list of lists, which was not indicated in the documentation. Hence, including as.list() liberally would run your example:

###
library(mirtCAT)

options <- matrix(c(1,2,3,4,5),
                  nrow = 3, ncol = 5, byrow = TRUE)
questions <- c("Building CATs with mirtCAT is difficult.",
               "mirtCAT requires a substantial amount of coding.",
               "I would use mirtCAT in my research.")

df<-data.frame(Question=questions,Option=options,Type="radio")

list.values<-vector(mode="list",length=3)
for(i in 1:3){

list.names[[i]]<-as.list(c("Strongly Disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly Agree"))
}

results<-mirtCAT(df=df, shinyGUI=list(choiceNames=list.names, choiceValues=list.values))
####

Typically these arguments are included for including more fancy HTML information, like the following, but it's really a matter of preference I suppose.

###
df2 <- df
choiceNames <- list(
    list(
        icon("calendar"),
        HTML("<p style='color:red;'>Red Text</p>"),
        "Normal text"),
    NULL, NULL
)
choiceValues = list(
    list("icon", "html", "text"), NULL, NULL)
results2 <- mirtCAT(df = df, shinyGUI = list(forced_choice = TRUE,
                                             choiceNames=choiceNames,
                                             choiceValues=choiceValues))
###

Phil
